cards.body:
## Summary
The money-authority rule that AGENTS.md states once is coded three times inside table-verify, and the copy the public verifier runs is the laxest. Fold them into one `authority.rs`: a closed `MoneyOp` (with the one path classifier) and one `judge(bundle, op) -> Result<why, why_not>` that both `verify_bundle` and the safety predicate call.

## Description
`lib.rs` `lawful` (:268) passes a clause-6 countersign on a Purchase, a seller mandate capture before the buyer approved, and a house mandate void. `safety.rs` `unlawful` (:109) refuses all three. Both sit in the same crate. The in-app safety record runs both, so the stricter one wins there. The judge-facing `table-verify` CLI and the in-app 'Check a proof file' (DECISIONS section 11) run only `lawful`, so a file can read VERIFIED when the wallet's own safety record would name a break in it. The path classifier (`operation_of` vs `money_kind`) and the owner-decision map (`decision_fits` vs `owner_decision_fits`) are also duplicated and already differ. The independent reading that matters, the verifier against table-app's pipeline, is kept. Only the verifier's copies of itself are merged.

## Flow
- Add `authority.rs`: `MoneyOp` {Create, Authorize, Capture, Void, InvoiceCreate, InvoiceSend} with `classify(method, path) -> Read | Op | Unclassified` (a query on a money POST is Unclassified), `decision_fits(decision, op)` and `judge(bundle, op_name, decided_by, reserved_seq)`, which is the conjunction of today's two rules. The owner.decision demand applies only on v2 files.
- `lib.rs` `closed`/`authority` call `judge`; `lawful`/`operation_of` are deleted.
- `safety.rs` `unlawful` and `money_kind` become thin wrappers so gauntlet.rs is unchanged; `owner_decision_fits` is deleted.
- `v2.rs` uses the shared classifier and `decision_fits`.

## Expected impact
The verifier a judge runs is exactly as strict as the gauntlet. This is the 'provable, not just trusted' claim of T1/ops-and-delivery-1. A future authority (a new DecidedBy or operation) is then added in one match, and every reader gets it.

## Evaluation
Claim: one rule, and the public verifier is no laxer than the safety predicate.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (cases 1-5 read ok=true; case 7 disagrees between the two classifiers; case 8's property fails on cases 1-5).
After: 8 of 8 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked lawful() against unlawful() for each DecidedBy branch (lib.rs:276-316 vs safety.rs:131-201) and the two path tables (lib.rs:323-334 vs safety.rs:78-90); the gate rung is the builder's.
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten. The offline verifier refuses more. No real wallet bundle changes verdict, because the gauntlet already holds every session to `unlawful` (STATUS.md:1762-1767), and v1 files keep their rule for Human steps. The safety.rs:424-427 assertion that a query'd capture is 'capture' is reversed on purpose.

cards.body:
## Summary
The owner signs wallet limits blind. The app already holds every buyer deal it would have judged, plus the exact pure check (`exposure_for_deal` + `WalletEnvelope::check`). Add `envelope_simulate`: the draft limits replayed over the last 7 days of purchases, before and after, shown above 'Sign with your owner key'. Fix the mandate what-if too: it claims 'allow' where the limits in force refuse.

## Description
T12 gave mandates a what-if. The wallet-wide limits (T14) sit above every mandate and can only refuse, but the sheet that sets them (WalletLimits.tsx:71-92) shows only today's meters. An owner choosing '2 deals a day' cannot tell that it would have stopped three of last Tuesday's purchases. The same gap makes the existing mandate what-if wrong: `simulate.rs` verdicts stop at `MandatePayload::check`, while the live `mandate_check_rounds` goes on to `envelope_check` (agent.rs:424). Any line the limits would refuse reads 'allow'. The new command reuses `SimulatedLine`/`MandateSimulation` (the verdict is `refuse{clause:0, reason}`, already the envelope's clause number), so the client renders it with the what-if components it already has.

## Flow
- `limits.rs`: pull the payload build and validation out of `sign_envelope` (`draft_envelope`) so the what-if refuses exactly as signing does.
- `simulate.rs`: `envelope_simulate(args)` over buyer deals in [from, to]. Per deal it uses `exposure_for_deal` at the deal's agreement place: `before` is the in-force envelope (none means allow), `after` is the draft. `mandate_simulate`'s two verdicts then also pass the in-force envelope when the mandate allows.
- The IPC row (approval, Read, OPEN), Action, dispatcher and shell handler; `generate-bindings`; PINNED_MANIFEST updated deliberately (AGENTS.md:64-73).
- WalletLimits sheet: a debounced what-if under the three fields: 'These limits would have stopped 2 of 9 purchases this week', listing only the changed lines. The mock mirrors it.

## Expected impact
A blind, high-stakes number becomes an informed one, and the Rules what-if stops overclaiming. Demo beat: drag 'deals a day' to 2 and watch Tuesday's third purchase turn coral before signing.

## Evaluation
Claim: the owner sees, before signing, every recorded purchase the new limits would refuse, and the rules what-if matches the live verdict under limits.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no envelope_simulate; case 5 reads allow)
After: 7 of 7 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked three same-day purchases through exposure_for_deal (exposure.rs:170-188) and check (:303-360) for max_deals_day 2 and max_out_day $80; the gate rung is the builder's.
Result: better
Gate: contract (a new in-repo IPC command; no external consumer). Note: DECISIONS section 40 item 6 froze IPC for the console rebuild. The coordinator should confirm that freeze ended with the rebuild.
